key_gap: Both converged on the same outcome (Hartford-line breach; Okafor cap ≈ $1.5M verdict EV; settlement ≈ $1.7–2.1M at mediation within ~90 days, contract-limited release + next-gen supply commitment), but the human modeled all four actors — including Heron Indemnity's misaligned incentives and Aurelia's three-claim precedent exposure — in a single opening pass, while the AI built the same actor map inside WHY and then underweighted Heron's incentive misalignment, correcting it only in HOW/REVIEW.
learning_signal: For outcome-prediction tasks in disputes, the sequence is actors-first: (1) enumerate every actor whose incentives touch the outcome — including hidden ones (insurers funding the defense, parallel pending claims that make precedent a first-order interest, counterparties with renewal leverage) — before doctrine; (2) model the decision-maker's institutional incentives (docket congestion, ADR mandates, precedents the decision-maker authored); (3) resolve split precedents by explicit fact-fit (mitigation shown vs. none); (4) compute each side's BATNA separately from legal EV — reservation prices (precedent exposure, covenant deadlines, renewal value) set the deal price, which can float above the capped verdict; (5) state the prediction with range, structure, and timing.
suggested_improvement: Add an 'actor-completeness pass' to WHY for outcome-prediction tasks: before doctrine, enumerate all parties with standing economic interests (including non-litigants: insurers, co-claimants on parallel disputes, renewal counterparties) and the decision-maker's institutional incentives; audit each actor's alignment with the party it nominally backs (Heron vs Aurelia); then resolve precedent splits by explicit fact-fit and price the settlement from the highest of each side's reservation values, not from legal EV. Require the first-pass actor map to pass a completeness check so incentive misalignment is caught in WHY, not in REVIEW.

key_gap: The pure style — adversarial cynicism, its registered weakness — modeled Halcyon (repeat litigant, delay as leverage), Brightleaf (litigation fatigue), and the docket (repeat-player familiarity) and advised accepting the 55% offer ($99k). It never opened the contract's 15-day objection clause, never registered 14 months of commercial use as factual acceptance/estoppel, and never touched the Small Business Prompt Payment Act — the statute that exists to make exactly Halcyon's delay game unprofitable (12% interest + mandatory fee-shifting). The AI checked the legal mechanism first, found the claim airtight, rejected the offer, and recommended the statutory demand → summary-judgment path for ≈ $210–220k.
learning_signal: When power and leverage look decisive, run a merits-first check before pricing the imbalance: (1) does the written record foreclose the counterparty's defense (acceptance clauses, lapsed objection windows, long commercial use of deliverables as factual acceptance)? (2) does any statute shift the delay economics (fee-shifting, statutory interest, prompt-payment acts)? (3) is there any genuine factual dispute at all (summary-judgment standard)? If the record is airtight and fees shift, the leverage belongs to the small party: serve the statutory demand, be ready to file SJ, and refuse discounts justified only by the other side's litigation capacity. A settlement price derived from power assumptions alone is the exact instrument the statute was written to confiscate.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'merits-first gate' to WHY for legal claims, preceding leverage/power analysis: (a) read the contract's acceptance and objection clauses and the fact record for acceptance-in-fact; (b) check the governing statute for fee-shifting/interest provisions that invert delay leverage; (c) test for any genuine factual dispute; (d) only then model actor power and litigation-fatigue risk, re-pricing the claim upward from the legal floor. Operational rule: 'if the defense is procedurally dead and fees shift to the losing party, the offered discount is a transfer, not a risk premium — reject it.'
